description: "The tenants KISS already holds for your locations, so you can reconcile them against your own records before you write. Each row carries both ids: your own `external_tenant_id` and the KISS `tenant_id` (a ULID). Rows with a null `external_tenant_id` are tenants KISS knows that you have not claimed — someone who signed up in the app, walked in, or arrived through another integration. Match those on `phone_number` and reuse the existing person rather than pushing a new id for them, which is what keeps you from creating a duplicate. Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with paging details in `meta.pagination`, and can be narrowed with `filter[location]`, `filter[external_location_code]`, or `filter[external_tenant_id]`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match`, so a periodic sweep can skip pages that have not changed. Needs the `tenants:read` scope."

The tenants KISS already holds for your locations, so you can reconcile them against your own records before you write. Each row carries both ids: your own `external_tenant_id` and the KISS `tenant_id` (a ULID). Rows with a null `external_tenant_id` are tenants KISS knows that you have not claimed — someone who signed up in the app, walked in, or arrived through another integration. Match those on `phone_number` and reuse the existing person rather than pushing a new id for them, which is what keeps you from creating a duplicate. Results are paged (15 per page, `per_page` up to 100) with paging details in `meta.pagination`, and can be narrowed with `filter[location]`, `filter[external_location_code]`, or `filter[external_tenant_id]`. Supports conditional requests via `ETag` / `If-None-Match`, so a periodic sweep can skip pages that have not changed. Needs the `tenants:read` scope.
